title: News Gapper
teaches: The News Gapper as we trade it: a fresh named catalyst, most often an earnings report, gaps a liquid stock up on at least three times its average volume; the gap holds and the day closes green in the upper half; the buy is the first pullback and reclaim, a market order as price trades over the prior day's high after two down days or an inside day that hold the gap-day low, or day one over the opening-range high for an A+; the stop sits a few cents under the pullback low, the first sell is a judgment, usually day 3 or later into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, with the rest on the 10-day or 21-day trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: In one line, what is a News Gapper?
choices: A gap on named news that holds
A gap on rumors that fills by lunch
A gap with no named news behind it
A small gap after a weak red close
questions.answer: A gap on named news that holds
questions.why: A gap on named news that holds. The catalyst is fresh and named, released outside market hours, most often a report, on a liquid stock. The gap holds when the day never trades back to the prior close and closes green in the upper half. A red close is not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: A News Gapper is a named catalyst gap that holds.

wrong.A gap on rumors that fills by lunch: A gap that fills is the opposite: that is a failed gap.
wrong.A gap with no named news behind it: Without a catalyst there is no News Gapper.
wrong.A small gap after a weak red close: That is a Kicker: a small gap on positioning, rarely a headline.

questions.q: A News Gapper needs a fresh, named catalyst; a big gap on no news is not one.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A News Gapper needs a fresh, named catalyst, released outside market hours and most often a report. A big gap on no news fails that test. Buying a gap with no catalyst, or a weak one such as an upgrade or a media mention, is a mistake.
questions.lesson_line: No named catalyst, no News Gapper.
questions.simple: True. A gap needs a fresh news reason that you can name, or it is not a News Gapper.

reasons: tied to held decision D-032 (catalyst types)

questions.q: What must the gap day do for the gap to count as holding?
choices: No fill, green close in upper half
Close at the exact high of day
Stay above its open all day
Close anywhere if volume is heavy
questions.answer: No fill, green close in upper half
questions.why: No fill, green close in the upper half. The day never trades back to the prior close and closes green in the upper half of its range. A lower-half close falls short and grades only a B-. A red close is not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: A held gap never revisits the prior close.

wrong.Close at the exact high of day: The close does not have to be the exact high; the upper half is the test.
wrong.Close anywhere if volume is heavy: Volume is its own test. A heavy day that closes in the lower half still misses the upper-half test.
wrong.Stay above its open all day: The test is the prior close, not the open. A day can dip under its open and still hold the gap.

questions.simple: A held gap never falls back to the prior close and ends the day green in the top half of its range.

deeper.counter: A gap can stay open and still be weak. NFLX, 2018: a 9.2% gap on 3.3x volume. The low of 35.65 stayed above the prior close of 34.64, so the gap never filled. But the day closed at 35% of its range, short of the upper-half test. Not filling is one test. The close is another.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card
the card says upper half for the key and also calls a lower-half close a B-, so the key follows the stricter line

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: On the pullback buy, the stop goes a few cents under the pullback ___.
questions.answer: low
questions.why: Low. On the pullback buy the stop goes a few cents under the pullback low.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the pullback low.

questions.q: Bonde made most of his big EP money buying pre-market, and we buy news gappers pre-market too.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. We buy at market in regular hours only, with no pre-market or after-hours buys. Bonde said he made most of his big EP money buying pre-market, but his habit is not our rule. Kullamagi also rarely trades extended hours and waits for the opening-range highs.
questions.lesson_line: No pre-market buys, even when Bonde made money there.
questions.simple: False. Bonde bought pre-market, but we only buy during regular trading hours.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (E58, no buys outside regular hours)

questions.q: News gappers work best in which market readings?
choices: Green or Yellow; size by grade
Orange or Red; fear drives gaps
Green only; Yellow is too risky
Any reading; headlines override it
questions.answer: Green or Yellow; size by grade
questions.why: Green or Yellow. Our market reading is a guide. Green is full risk per grade and Yellow is smaller and fewer. Orange allows only A+ setups, and Red is mostly cash and shorts. A good headline does not change the reading.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first: Green or Yellow for gappers.

wrong.Orange or Red; fear drives gaps: Orange allows only A+ setups, and Red is mostly cash and shorts.
wrong.Green only; Yellow is too risky: Yellow is allowed too, smaller and fewer.
wrong.Any reading; headlines override it: A good headline does not switch the market reading off.

questions.simple: Green or Yellow. UCT takes full or smaller risk there, but only A+ setups in Orange and mostly cash in Red.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (F65 market reading)

questions.q: Earnings gaps cluster in about 3 to 4 weeks of each quarter.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The gaps cluster in 3 to 4 weeks of earnings season each quarter, so those are the weeks to watch.
questions.lesson_line: Gaps cluster in earnings season. Watch those weeks.
questions.simple: True. Earnings gaps bunch up in a few weeks each quarter, so watch those weeks.

reasons: one cited fact only (our card)
a timing claim about the calendar that can change

questions.q: How much volume does a News Gapper need by the close?
choices: At least 3 times the 50-day average
Any volume if the gap is big
Just above the 50-day average
Less than the 50-day average
questions.answer: At least 3 times the 50-day average
questions.why: At least 3 times the 50-day average, and on pace for it by the opening-range buy. Kullamagi: volume is the number one thing to focus on.
questions.lesson_line: Three times average volume is the line.

wrong.Any volume if the gap is big: A big gap on thin volume is the trap; volume is the line.
wrong.Just above the 50-day average: Just above average is the B- zone, below the line.
wrong.Less than the 50-day average: Below average volume is the opposite of a news gap.

questions.q: The pullback buy waits for two down days or an inside day whose closes all hold the gap-day low.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. After two down days or an inside day that keep every close above the gap-day low, the buy is a market order over the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: The pullback must hold the gap-day low on every close.

questions.q: In the first ten sessions, which event ends the setup?
choices: A close under the gap-day low
An inside day
Two down days that hold the low
A quiet day on lighter volume
questions.answer: A close under the gap-day low
questions.why: A close under the gap-day low. The gap fills or the stock closes under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low ends it.

wrong.An inside day: An inside day is a pullback pattern we want.
wrong.Two down days that hold the low: Two down days that hold the gap-day low are the pullback itself.
wrong.A quiet day on lighter volume: A quiet day on lighter volume is part of a healthy pullback.

questions.q: A gap on good news that closes red is a News Failure, not a News Gapper.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A red close after good news is the News Failure. Same headline, opposite trade.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, red close: a different trade.

questions.q: Which headline is the strongest catalyst?
choices: A beat with a raised outlook
A mention on a morning TV show
One analyst upgrade to a buy
A vague press release about plans
questions.answer: A beat with a raised outlook
questions.why: An earnings beat with a raised outlook. Our card rates earnings with a beat and a raise among the strongest catalysts. Bonde: earnings, new products and raised guidance have a high probability of starting multi-month rallies. Media mentions and analyst upgrades have a low probability of follow-through. Buying a gap on a weak catalyst is a mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings with a raise beats a mention or an upgrade.

wrong.A mention on a morning TV show: A media mention has a low probability of follow-through.
wrong.One analyst upgrade to a buy: An analyst upgrade has a low probability of follow-through.
wrong.A vague press release about plans: A vague press release is a B- catalyst, not a strong one.

questions.simple: A beat with a raised outlook is strongest. Earnings news can start a long rally, but mentions and upgrades rarely follow through.

reasons: tied to held decision D-032 (catalyst types)

questions.q: When do we skip a news gapper's pullback buy?
choices: A report is due within 3 sessions
The stock is up on the day
Volume is above average
The market is Green
questions.answer: A report is due within 3 sessions
questions.why: A report is due within 3 sessions. We take no new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report.
questions.lesson_line: No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

wrong.The stock is up on the day: Being up on the day is how a reclaim looks.
wrong.Volume is above average: Above-average volume is a plus for a gapper.
wrong.The market is Green: Green is the reading we want.

questions.q: For an earnings gap, the fundamentals decide the grade before the chart is looked at.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. For an earnings gap, growing sales and earnings, ideally accelerating, with a beat and raised guidance, are a grade cue. We prefer growing sales and earnings, but the chart comes first. The cue adds to the grade. It does not replace the chart.
questions.lesson_line: Fundamentals are a cue. The chart decides.
questions.simple: False. The chart comes first, and growing sales and earnings only help the grade.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (D40, the chart comes first)

questions.q: On a news gapper you may add shares when volume surges after the buy.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The full size goes in at one price with one stop, with no adding. A surge in volume after the buy does not change that. The stop sets the size before you buy, and adding later would break the size the stop set.
questions.lesson_line: One buy, one price, one stop.
questions.simple: False. You buy the full size once, at one price, with one stop, and you do not add.

reasons: one cited fact only (rulebook A5)
rests on the owner's rulebook

questions.q: Bought at 105.11 with the stop at 103.20. Where is 3R?
questions.why: $110.84. One R is the fill minus the stop, 105.11 minus 103.20. Add three of those to the 105.11 fill. 3R is a measuring mark, not a fixed sell.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. It is a measuring mark, not a sell order.
questions.simple: 3R is 110.84. One R is the fill minus the stop, and 3R sits three of those above the fill.

deeper.example: TGT was bought at 105.11 with the stop at 103.20, a stop 1.8% away. It ran to 12.0R. So 3R at 110.84 was only a mark on the way.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (B19 first trim)

wrong.$108.93: Added three R to the stop, not the fill.
wrong.$99.38: Subtracted three R from the fill.

questions.q: Gap day: low 100.00, high 110.00, close 107.00. Where in the range did it close, from 0 to 1?
questions.why: 0.70. The close minus the low is 107 minus 100. Divide that by the range, 110 minus 100. That is in the upper half, so this day meets the close test for a held gap. A held gap also needs the day never to trade back to the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Close minus low, over the range. Upper half passes the close test.
questions.simple: The close is 0.70 of the way up the range. That is the upper half.

reasons: a computed key

wrong.0.30: Measured down from the high, not up from the low.
wrong.0.97: Divided the close by the high and skipped the low.
wrong.0.07: Divided by the low, not by the range.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on the pullback buy?
choices: A few cents under the pullback low
Under the gap-day low, however far
At the prior close, the gap-fill price
1% under the pullback low for room
questions.answer: A few cents under the pullback low
questions.why: A few cents under the pullback low. We set the stop first and size from it. The gap-day low is the line a close must hold, not the stop. There is no porosity: the stop is the exit and it only moves up. On day one the stop goes a few cents under the day's low at the buy.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits under the pullback low.

wrong.Under the gap-day low, however far: The gap-day low is the line a close must hold. The stop is a few cents under the pullback low.
wrong.At the prior close, the gap-fill price: The prior close is the gap-fill price. The stop goes a few cents under the pullback low, not there.
wrong.1% under the pullback low for room: No porosity: the stop is a few cents under the low, not a 1% cushion.

questions.simple: Put the stop a few cents under the pullback low, because the stop is the exit and gets no cushion.

reasons: the stop rule is the owner's rulebook default (F62)

questions.q: What is left trails a close under the 20 EMA for a fast mover or the 9 EMA for a steadier one.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. It is the other way round. Sell on a close under the 9 EMA for a fast mover or the 20 EMA for a steadier one. The sell is on a close below the average, not an intraday dip.
questions.lesson_line: Trail what is left under the 9 or 20 EMA.
questions.simple: False. A fast mover is trailed on the 9 EMA and a steadier stock on the 20 EMA.

reasons: the trail pairing is the owner's rulebook default (E52), and the question swaps the pair

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: We often sell into a 3, 5 or ___ day push.
questions.why: 7. We often sell into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, or at about 5 to 10R. The first sell is a judgment, not a fixed third at 3R. The rest can trail the 9 EMA or the 20 EMA.
questions.lesson_line: A 3, 5 or 7 day push is often the place for the first sell.
questions.simple: We often sell into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, and the first sell is a judgment call.

reasons: the trim levels are the owner's rulebook defaults (E51) and are marked adjustable

questions.q: Which gap is an A+ gap?
choices: 10% or more, and a true gap
10% or more, filled or not
Any gap on 3x usual volume
Any gap that closes green
questions.answer: 10% or more, and a true gap
questions.why: 10% or more, and a true gap. A true gap means the day's low stays above the prior day's high. ChartSchool says the same for an up gap. A gap that fills fails that test.
questions.lesson_line: A+ gap: ten percent or more, and a true gap.

wrong.10% or more, filled or not: A true gap keeps the day's low above the prior day's high. A gap that fills does not.
wrong.Any gap on 3x usual volume: Volume is its own test. The A+ gap is judged on its size and on being a true gap.
wrong.Any gap that closes green: A green close is needed for any gapper. The A+ gap also needs 10% or more and a true gap.

questions.simple: An A+ gap is 10% or more and a true gap, so the day's low stays above the prior day's high.

reasons: the 10% line is a proposed card number, held under D-033
the card is the only source for the A+ size

questions.q: A true gap means the day's low stays above the prior day's high.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. For an up gap, the low must be higher than the previous day's high.
questions.lesson_line: A true gap leaves a hole above yesterday's high.

questions.q: The 50-day average volume is 4 million shares. The gap day trades 13 million. What is the multiple?
questions.why: 3.25x. Divide gap-day volume by the 50-day average: 13 million over 4 million. That clears the line of at least 3 times. The line is for the close, and the stock must be on pace for it by the buy.
questions.lesson_line: Volume multiple is today over the 50-day average.
questions.simple: Divide 13 million by 4 million to get 3.25, which clears the line of at least 3 times.

reasons: computed key
the 3 times line is a proposed card number

wrong.0.31x: Flipped it: divided the average by the gap-day volume.
wrong.2.25x: Used the extra volume over the average, not the whole day.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A stock gapped 12% on a contract headline, on heavy volume, and closed strong. Two down days followed, both closing above the gap-day low. This morning it trades over yesterday's high.
choices: Market buy; stop below pullback low
Pass; day one was the only entry
Wait for the gap to fill, then buy
Limit buy at gap-day low; stop under
questions.answer: Market buy; stop below pullback low
questions.why: Buy at market. After two down days that hold the gap-day low, buy as price trades over the prior day's high. The stop goes a few cents under the pullback low. The gap-day low is the line that must hold. It is not the stop.
questions.lesson_line: Buy as price trades over the prior day's high.

wrong.Pass; day one was the only entry: The pullback buy is the entry here; day one is not the only one.
wrong.Wait for the gap to fill, then buy: A gap that trades back to the prior close has failed. The setup needs the gap to hold.
wrong.Limit buy at gap-day low; stop under: A limit at the gap-day low sits under the market and misses the trigger over the prior high.

questions.simple: Buy at market as price trades over the prior day's high, with the stop a few cents under the pullback low.

reasons: tied to held decision D-033 (gap floor; story gap moved to 12%)
fixed before

questions.q: Is there a buy?
questions.story: The pullback closes under the gap-day low on day 3. On day 4 the stock rallies and trades over the prior day's high.
choices: No; the setup ended on day 3
Yes; the reclaim is the trigger
Yes, at half size to cut the risk
Wait; a higher close revives it
questions.answer: No; the setup ended on day 3
questions.why: No. The pullback closed under the gap-day low on day 3, before any reclaim, so there is no Buy 2. A close under the gap-day low in the first 10 sessions ends the setup. The day-4 rally does not undo that.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback that breaks the gap-day low has no buy.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim is the trigger: The reclaim only counts if the pullback held the gap-day low.
wrong.Yes, at half size to cut the risk: Half size cuts the risk, but a broken setup is still broken.
wrong.Wait; a higher close revives it: The setup is invalidated. A higher close does not undo a close under the gap-day low.

questions.simple: No. A close under the gap-day low ended the setup, so the rally on day 4 is not a buy.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card
the invalidation line is a proposed card criterion

questions.q: Buy or pass?
questions.story: The reclaim level is 40.00. You were away from your desk, and at 10:30 the stock trades 41.80.
choices: Pass; buying here is chasing
Buy, the reclaim is confirmed
Buy half size to cut the risk
Buy with a wider stop to fit it in
questions.answer: Pass; buying here is chasing
questions.why: Pass. 41.80 is more than 4% over the 40.00 reclaim level, and we never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink. If a day gaps past the level, a morning flush that curls back up is another way in.
questions.lesson_line: Miss it rather than chase it. A morning flush that curls back up can be another way in.

wrong.Buy, the reclaim is confirmed: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Buy half size to cut the risk: We never buy more than 4% above the buy point, at any size.
wrong.Buy with a wider stop to fit it in: The stop stays under the buy point. A wider stop does not remove the 4% line.

questions.simple: Pass, because 41.80 is more than 4% over the 40.00 reclaim, and we never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

deeper.trap: It is tempting to think a smaller buy or a wider stop repairs a late entry. It does not. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink. At 41.80 against a 40.00 reclaim, the answer is to pass.

reasons: the 4% chase line is the owner's rulebook (C28)
the reference level (reclaim or base pivot) is held under D-022

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A contract headline hits at 7:30 am. The stock is up 11% pre-market on big volume.
choices: Wait for the opening range, then decide
Buy now with a market order
Buy half now, half at the open
Place a stop-limit just under the gap
questions.answer: Wait for the opening range, then decide
questions.why: Wait. We never buy before the open. The opening range forms first, and the day-one buy, if any, comes over its high in regular hours.
questions.lesson_line: No pre-market buys. Let the opening range form.

wrong.Buy now with a market order: Entries are market orders in regular hours, not pre-market.
wrong.Buy half now, half at the open: Half a pre-market buy is still a pre-market buy.
wrong.Place a stop-limit just under the gap: A stop-limit under the gap is not an entry plan.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: Your news gapper is up 7R after four straight up days. Two of them were gap ups, and each day's range was wider than the last.
choices: Sell a big part into the run-up
Hold it all; the trail is the exit
Add; momentum is strongest here
Sell everything at the open tomorrow
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the run-up
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. Three to five straight up days with gaps and range expansion is a climax run. Four straight up days, two of them gaps, each range wider than the last, fits. Selling a big part is a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: A climax run is the time to sell a big part.

wrong.Add; momentum is strongest here: No adding: the full size goes in at one price with one stop.
wrong.Sell everything at the open tomorrow: The rule says sell a big part, a judgment call, not everything.
wrong.Hold it all; the trail is the exit: A climax run is a judgment call to sell a big part, not to hold it all.

questions.simple: A climax run of straight up days with gaps and wider ranges is the time to sell a big part.

deeper.trap: The trap is thinking the strongest move is the safest to hold or add to. Three to five straight up days with gaps and range expansion is a climax run. Buying the third gap of a parabolic burst is also a listed mistake. Strength here is the reason to sell a big part.

reasons: the climax sale is a judgment call in the owner's rulebook (C34)

questions.q: How do you handle the first sell here?
questions.story: You bought at 50.00 this morning with the stop at 48.00, so 3R is 56.00. By 2:00 the stock trades at 56.00.
choices: Hold; we rarely sell on day 1
Sell a third now at 3R, 56.00
Sell it all now, 56.00
Sell half now and raise the stop
questions.answer: Hold; we rarely sell on day 1
questions.why: Hold. We very rarely sell on day 1 of the buy, even at 3R. We usually wait until day 3 at the earliest. The first sell is a judgment, not a fixed third at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: 3R on day 1 is not a sell signal. Wait for day 3 at the earliest.

wrong.Sell a third now at 3R, 56.00: A fixed third at 3R is not our rule. The first sell is a judgment.
wrong.Sell it all now, 56.00: Selling everything on day 1 misses the multi-week trend. We rarely sell on day 1.
wrong.Sell half now and raise the stop: Half is still a day-1 sell. We usually wait until day 3 at the earliest.

questions.simple: Hold. We very rarely sell on day 1, even at 3R, and we wait until day 3 at the earliest.

reasons: the open-trim rule is the owner's rulebook (F63)

questions.q: On a news gapper the stop may move to breakeven anywhere from 2R to 5R.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Ideally the stop moves to breakeven somewhere between 2R and 5R. The stop only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven anywhere from 2R to 5R, then the stop only moves up.
questions.simple: True. The stop can move to breakeven anywhere from 2R to 5R, then it only moves up, apart from the gap rule.

reasons: the rulebook gives a range of 2R to 5R, and the first-trim default is the card's

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: The stock gapped 9% on a report. At 9:50 it trades over the 5-minute high, still above its open. It has already traded its full average daily volume. The day's low is 2% under the price.
choices: Buy at market, stop under day's low
Pass; day one is not a buy here
Half now, half at close; one stop
Buy tomorrow's open; stop at low
questions.answer: Buy at market, stop under day's low
questions.why: Buy at market. Day one over the opening-range high is the A+ form, and the pullback and reclaim is the other way in. Volume is hot, with the average daily volume already traded. The stop goes a few cents under the day's low, about 2% away.
questions.lesson_line: Day one over the opening-range high is the A+ form.

wrong.Pass; day one is not a buy here: Day one over the opening-range high with hot volume is a buy we teach, the A+ form.
wrong.Half now, half at close; one stop: Half now and half later is two prices, not one buy.
wrong.Buy tomorrow's open; stop at low: Waiting for tomorrow's open gives up the trigger that fired today.

questions.simple: Buy at market as price trades over the opening-range high. Put the stop a few cents under the day's low.

reasons: rests on held decision D-086 (day one against the reclaim)
also D-005 (day-one stop)
fixed before

questions.q: Which lesson owns the day, and which the pullback buy?
questions.story: The gap day is a report's reaction day on an established leader clearing a four-month base.
choices: PEG owns the day; we teach the buy
We own the day and the buy both
Gap Support owns first pullback
Episodic Pivot owns day; no buy
questions.answer: PEG owns the day; we teach the buy
questions.why: The PEG owns the day. The pullback buy is taught here. A report's reaction day on an established leader clearing its base is the PEG. The first-pullback entry on either is taught here. An Episodic Pivot is the first gap in six months on a neglected name.
questions.lesson_line: A report day on a leader is a PEG. The pullback entry is taught here.

wrong.We own the day and the buy both: The PEG lesson owns a report reaction day on a leader.
wrong.Gap Support owns first pullback: Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low, not the first pullback.
wrong.Episodic Pivot owns day; no buy: An Episodic Pivot is a neglected name, not a leader clearing a base.

questions.simple: The PEG lesson owns the report day on a leader, and this lesson teaches the pullback buy on either kind of gap.

reasons: tied to held decision D-002 (scope of this lesson)
fixed before

questions.q: News Gapper or News Failure?
questions.story: A contract headline gaps a stock up 8% at the open. By the close it is 2% under the prior close.
choices: A News Failure; the opposite trade
A News Gapper; the headline was good
A News Gapper; buy the pullback
A Kicker; the close was weak
questions.answer: A News Failure; the opposite trade
questions.why: A News Failure. A gapper holds its gap and closes green in the upper half. This stock gapped up on good news and closed under the prior close, so the gap failed. Same headline, opposite trade.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, red close: the opposite trade.

wrong.A News Gapper; the headline was good: Good news does not make a gap hold. The close decides.
wrong.A News Gapper; buy the pullback: A close under the prior close is not a gap that held.
wrong.A Kicker; the close was weak: A Kicker needs a weak red close the day before the gap.

questions.simple: A gap that closes under the prior close has failed, so this is a News Failure, not a News Gapper.

deeper.counter: Good news does not decide it. The close does. A gap that holds closes green in the upper half. One that closes under the prior close is a News Failure, even on the same headline. Check the close before you call the headline good.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card
the News Failure trade is not taught here (D-001)

questions.q: Which setup is it?
questions.story: Monday ends with a weak red close. Tuesday opens 2% higher on 1.6x volume with no headline.
choices: A Kicker; a small gap on positioning
A News Gapper; 1.6x is enough
A PEG; the stock gapped on volume
An Episodic Pivot; weak close
questions.answer: A Kicker; a small gap on positioning
questions.why: A Kicker. It needs a weak red close and then a gap of only 1.5% or more on positioning, rarely a headline. Monday closed weak and red, and Tuesday gapped 2% with no news. A News Gapper needs a named catalyst and at least 3 times volume. This had 1.6x.
questions.lesson_line: A weak red close and a small gap with no news is a Kicker.

wrong.A News Gapper; 1.6x is enough: A News Gapper needs a named catalyst and at least 3 times volume. This had no headline and 1.6x.
wrong.A PEG; the stock gapped on volume: A PEG is a report's reaction day on a leader. This gap came with no headline.
wrong.An Episodic Pivot; weak close: An Episodic Pivot is the first gap in six months on a neglected name. Nothing here says that.

questions.simple: A Kicker is a small gap after a weak red close, rarely on news. This one had no headline and only 1.6x volume.

reasons: the Kicker line comes from one criteria card
the lookalike tells are proposed card criteria

questions.q: News Gapper or Gap Support?
questions.story: Five weeks after a report gap, the stock dips to the gap-up low, undercuts it slightly, and closes back over it.
choices: Gap Support, the later test
A News Gapper pullback buy
A News Failure; the gap broke
A PEG; it is an earnings stock
questions.answer: Gap Support, the later test
questions.why: Gap Support. The gapper's pullback stays above the gap-day low and reclaims within about ten sessions. Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low itself, bought as that low is defended. Five weeks on, this is the later test.
questions.lesson_line: A test of the gap-up low weeks later is Gap Support.

wrong.A News Gapper pullback buy: The News Gapper pullback comes within about ten sessions and stays above the gap-day low.
wrong.A News Failure; the gap broke: A News Failure is a red close on day one, not a test weeks later.
wrong.A PEG; it is an earnings stock: A PEG is the report's reaction day, not a test five weeks on.

questions.simple: It is Gap Support because the dip came weeks later and tested the gap-up low itself, not the first pullback.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: What makes this gap an Episodic Pivot and not an ordinary gapper?
questions.story: A stock nobody follows has been flat for six months. A contract headline gaps it 18% on 9x volume, the first gap in a year.
choices: First gap in six months, neglected name
The 18% size of the gap on the day
The contract headline behind the move
The 9x volume that traded on the gap day
questions.answer: First gap in six months, neglected name
questions.why: An EP is the first gap in six months, on a neglected name. This stock was flat for six months, and the gap was its first in a year. Size, volume and a headline fit an ordinary gapper too.
questions.lesson_line: An EP is a first gap in six months on a neglected name.

wrong.The 18% size of the gap on the day: A gapper can gap that far too. A gap of 10% or more is the A+ gap.
wrong.The contract headline behind the move: A News Gapper has a named catalyst too. The EP tell is neglect.
wrong.The 9x volume that traded on the gap day: A News Gapper can have big volume too. The EP tell is neglect.

questions.simple: An Episodic Pivot is the first gap in six months or more on a neglected name.

reasons: the lookalike tell comes from one criteria card
whether an EP is a version of the News Gapper is held under D-002

questions.q: Which stock earns the A+ cue for how it moved before the gap?
questions.story: Two 11% gaps on record volume. One is on a stock flat for three months. The other is on a stock up 25% in three months.
choices: Only the first; it was quiet before
Both; both have record volume
Only the second; it has momentum now
Neither; an 11% gap is too small
questions.answer: Only the first; it was quiet before
questions.why: Only the first. Quiet before the gap, not up more than about 15% in 3 months, is an A+ cue. The second ran 25% in 3 months, so it lacks it. Both gaps are 11% on record volume.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet before the gap is an A+ cue.

wrong.Neither; an 11% gap is too small: A gap of 10% or more is an A+ gap, so 11% is not small.
wrong.Both; both have record volume: Record volume is the same for both. The quiet-before-the-gap cue is not.
wrong.Only the second; it has momentum now: A run into the gap is not an A+ cue. Quiet before the gap is.

questions.simple: Only the flat stock gets the quiet-before-the-gap cue. The stock up 25% in three months does not.

deeper.example: Same gap, same volume, different months before it. Quiet before the gap is an A+ cue: not up more than about 15% in 3 months. The stock up 25% misses that cue. Up 30% or more already is a B- cue.

reasons: the 15% and 30% lines are proposed card numbers, held under D-033
all cited facts come from one criteria card

questions.q: Grade each close.
questions.story: Same gap, same volume, two stocks, and both hold the gap. One closes at 93% of its range. The other closes at 60%.
choices: First an A+ cue; second just holds
Both the same; held the gap
First just holds; second A+ cue
Both A+; both green and held
questions.answer: First an A+ cue; second just holds
questions.why: The first is an A+ cue, and the second just holds the gap. A close in the top quarter of the range is an A+ cue, and 93% is in it. A close in the upper half holds the gap but is not an A+ cue, and 60% is there. The close separates them.
questions.lesson_line: Top-quarter close is an A+ cue. Upper half just holds the gap.

wrong.Both the same; held the gap: Both held the gap, but only the 93% close is in the top quarter, an A+ cue.
wrong.First just holds; second A+ cue: It is the other way round: only the 93% close is in the top quarter, the A+ cue.
wrong.Both A+; both green and held: Only a top-quarter close is the A+ cue, and 60% is not.

questions.simple: The 93% close is an A+ cue because it sits in the top quarter. The 60% close only holds the gap.

reasons: fixed before
grading cues vs the rulebook's E50 (grading is discretionary): flagged to the owner

questions.q: Grade the catalyst of each.
questions.story: Two stocks gap 12% on 4x volume. One gaps on a government contract. The other gaps on an analyst upgrade.
choices: Contract stronger; upgrade is weak
Both A+; the gap and volume match
Upgrade stronger; analysts move stocks
Same grade; a gap is still a gap
questions.answer: Contract stronger; upgrade is weak
questions.why: The contract is stronger. A government contract is a named catalyst. An upgrade is a weak one: Bonde says upgrades have a low probability of follow-through. Buying a gap on a weak catalyst is a mistake. The gap and volume match, so the catalyst decides.
questions.lesson_line: A named contract beats an analyst upgrade as a catalyst.

wrong.Both A+; the gap and volume match: The catalyst is what differs, and an upgrade is weak.
wrong.Upgrade stronger; analysts move stocks: An upgrade has a low probability of follow-through.
wrong.Same grade; a gap is still a gap: Both gaps are the same size; the catalyst is what differs.

questions.simple: The contract is stronger because an upgrade is a weak catalyst that often does not follow through.

reasons: tied to held decisions D-032 and D-033
fixed before

questions.q: Account 40,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 105.11, stop 103.20. How many shares?
questions.answer: 104 shares
questions.why: 104 shares. Risk dollars are 0.5% of 40,000. Divide that by the fill minus the stop, 105.11 minus 103.20, and round down. The stop sets the size. Then the size is the smaller of this and the position cap.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.
questions.simple: 104 shares. Multiply the account by the risk percent, divide by the gap between fill and stop, and round down.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (A5 sizing)
fixed before

choices: 382 shares
10 shares
209 shares
104 shares

wrong.10 shares: Slipped the decimal: used a tenth of the risk percent.
wrong.382 shares: Multiplied by the stop distance instead of dividing.

questions.q: Buy the reclaim?
questions.story: A news gap on Monday, a clean pullback, and a reclaim that triggers on Thursday. The company reports Friday after the close.
choices: No; the report is too close to buy
Yes; the reclaim is perfect
No; day 4 is too early to reclaim
Yes, and hold it through the report
questions.answer: No; the report is too close to buy
questions.why: No. A news gapper with a report due within 3 sessions waits. We take no new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. The reclaim triggers Thursday and the report comes Friday after the close, so the buy sits inside the window. Holding through a report is allowed only when the trade is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: With a report in the next 3 sessions, no new buy.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim is perfect: The rule bars new buys in the 3 days before a report, whatever the chart looks like.
wrong.Yes, and hold it through the report: Holding through a report needs the trade up 5R, and a new buy is not.
wrong.No; day 4 is too early to reclaim: Day 4 is the earliest reclaim the rule allows after a two-day pullback, so Thursday is on time.

questions.simple: No, because a report is due Friday and we take no new buys in the 3 days before a report.

reasons: the 3-day report window is the owner's rulebook (B22)

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: Seven sessions after the gap, the stock closes under the gap-day low. You have not bought yet.
choices: Off; no Buy 2
Keep waiting for a deeper pullback
Buy at the close; it is cheap
On; only a gap fill ends it
questions.answer: Off; no Buy 2
questions.why: Off. A close under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions invalidates the setup. There is nothing to buy.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low ends it.

wrong.Keep waiting for a deeper pullback: The gap-day low gave way on a close. Waiting does not undo that.
wrong.Buy at the close; it is cheap: Buying cheaper is not the test; the line has to hold.
wrong.On; only a gap fill ends it: A close under the gap-day low also ends it.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
questions.story: A friend quotes Morales and Kacher and says to allow a little room: put the stop 2% under the pullback low.
choices: Just under the pullback low
2% under the pullback low
Under the low of the gap day
At the prior day's close
questions.answer: Just under the pullback low
questions.why: A few cents under the pullback low, not 2% under it. Morales and Kacher allow a 1 to 2% undercut of the gap-up low in some cases. We do not copy that. There is no porosity: the stop is the exit and it only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: No porosity. The stop is the exit.

wrong.2% under the pullback low: That copies their porosity. Our stop is a few cents under a real low.
wrong.At the prior day's close: The prior close is the gap-fill price. Our stop is a few cents under the pullback low.
wrong.Under the low of the gap day: The gap-day low is the line a close must hold, not our stop.

questions.simple: Put the stop a few cents under the pullback low. Our stop is the exit, so it gets no extra room.

reasons: teaches the owner's no-porosity stop over a published web view (Morales and Kacher)
the stop rule is the owner's rulebook default (F62)

questions.q: Our Sunday Scans say that, coming out of a correction, the recent earnings gappers usually lag the market.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Our Sunday Scans say the opposite: coming out of a correction, the recent earnings gappers often have stellar performance on the other side. Often is not always, and any buy still needs its own trigger.
questions.lesson_line: After a correction, watch the recent earnings gappers.
questions.simple: False. After a correction, the newest earnings gappers often lead the next move up.

reasons: rests on the owner's published Sunday Scans line and the card that copies it

questions.q: Take the reclaim?
questions.story: A gapper on a contract jumped 20% and held the gap. After a clean pullback, the reclaim level is $8. The stock usually trades about $6 million a day.
choices: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
Yes; the gap day's volume is huge
No; a 20% gap is too late to buy
Yes; an $8 stock is cheap enough to size
questions.answer: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: No. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. This one is $8 and trades about $6 million a day, so it fails both tests. A great gap does not change the liquidity rule. We also never own more than 1% of average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars and twenty million a day, or we skip.

wrong.Yes; the gap day's volume is huge: One big day does not fix the price: $8 is under the $10 line.
wrong.No; a 20% gap is too late to buy: The answer is no, but not for that reason. Gap size is not the test here. Price and dollar volume are.
wrong.Yes; an $8 stock is cheap enough to size: Both the price and the dollar volume fail.

questions.simple: No. The stock is under $10 and trades under $20 million a day, so we skip it however good the gap looks.

deeper.counter: One big volume day does not help. The price rule fails on its own: at $8 the stock is under the $10 line. Its usual $6 million a day also misses the $20 million line.

reasons: tied to held decision D-030 (liquidity)
rests on the owner's rulebook (B23)
fixed before

questions.q: Fill 33.55, stop 32.59. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 2.9%. The fill minus the stop is 33.55 minus 32.59. Divide that by the fill, 33.55, and show it as a percent. That sits inside the usual 3%, because our stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy. It is a loss on the position, not on the account.
questions.lesson_line: Stop distance is the fill minus the stop, over the fill.
questions.simple: 2.9. The gap between fill and stop is a small slice of the fill price, inside the usual 3%.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (A13, the 3% habit)

wrong.97.1%: Divided the stop by the fill and skipped the subtraction.
wrong.28.6%: Decimal slip: ten times too big.
wrong.96.0%: Turned the dollar gap into a percent without dividing by the fill.

questions.q: Hold or sell?
questions.story: You hold a news gapper that is up 4R. The next report is tomorrow after the close.
choices: Sell before the report; under 5R
Sell all; a report needs 10R to hold
Hold; the last report was a winner
Hold; the stop covers a report gap
questions.answer: Sell before the report; under 5R
questions.why: Sell before the report. We hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R, and this one is up 4R. The last news says nothing about the next report.
questions.lesson_line: Under 5R going into a report, sell first.

wrong.Hold; the last report was a winner: The last news says nothing about the next report.
wrong.Hold; the stop covers a report gap: A stop can be gapped through, so it does not cover a report.
wrong.Sell all; a report needs 10R to hold: Selling is right, but the line to hold is 5R, not 10R.

questions.simple: Sell before the report, because a trade up only 4R does not clear the 5R needed to hold through one.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B22 report rule)
fixed before

questions.q: What was that loss?
questions.story: AVAV, 2024. A 15.3% gap on 15.8x volume closed at 79% of its range. You bought the 8-session pullback and reclaim at 162.59. It went straight to the stop at 158.43.
choices: A planned loss; the stop did its job
A bad gap; never a real gapper
A sign the setup no longer works
A broken rule; stop too tight
questions.answer: A planned loss; the stop did its job
questions.why: A planned loss; the stop did its job. The gap was strong: 15.3% on 15.8x volume, closing at 79% of its range. The pullback was bought at 162.59 and went straight to the stop at 158.43 without a single higher high. A big-volume gap does not protect the buy.
questions.lesson_line: A big-volume gap does not protect a pullback buy. The stop does.

wrong.A bad gap; never a real gapper: The gap was big, on heavy volume, and closed at 79% of its range.
wrong.A sign the setup no longer works: Only about three in ten reach 3R before the stop. One stopped trade does not retire the setup.
wrong.A broken rule; stop too tight: The stop sits a few cents under the pullback low, not wherever gives more room. A stop that is hit is not a rule break.

questions.simple: It was a planned loss. A strong gap does not protect a pullback buy, and the stop got us out.

deeper.example: AVAV, 2024: a 15.3% gap on 15.8x volume, closing at 79% of its range. The 8-session pullback was bought at 162.59 and went straight to the stop at 158.43. Compare TWLO: also bought on pullback day 8, it ran to 24.1R. The stop is what makes both outcomes acceptable.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed
keyed on the stop rule, not on when the reclaim came

questions.q: Where does the pullback buy fail most often?
choices: Early reclaim after a wide day-one bar
A reclaim after a quiet 4-day pullback
A reclaim on a clean inside day
A reclaim that holds the upper half
questions.answer: Early reclaim after a wide day-one bar
questions.why: An early reclaim after a very wide day-one bar. Three of the four losing reclaims came on day 4, the earliest after a two-session pullback.
questions.lesson_line: Beware the early reclaim after a very wide first day.

wrong.A reclaim after a quiet 4-day pullback: A quiet pullback that holds the low is the good version.
wrong.A reclaim on a clean inside day: An inside day that holds the gap-day low is a good pullback.
wrong.A reclaim that holds the upper half: Holding the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue.

questions.q: What does the plan do ten sessions after the buy?
questions.story: PEN, 2026. An 11.1% gap on 18.2x volume, in a stock already up 23.8% over 65 sessions. You bought the day-4 reclaim at 357.70, and it has drifted under 1R since.
choices: Sells it and frees up the money
Holds it; the stop has not been hit
Adds to it; the stock is coiling
Holds it until the 20 EMA breaks
questions.answer: Sells it and frees up the money
questions.why: It sells the trade. The time stop: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. This reclaim reached only 0.45R and drifted. The plan does not wait for the stop to be hit.
questions.lesson_line: Under 1R after ten sessions, the trade is sold.

wrong.Holds it; the stop has not been hit: The time stop exists for exactly this trade.
wrong.Adds to it; the stock is coiling: Adding breaks one buy, one price, one stop.
wrong.Holds it until the 20 EMA breaks: The trail is for what is left. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold.

questions.simple: It sells, because a trade still under 1R after ten sessions is sold to free the money.

deeper.example: PEN gapped 11.1% on 18.2x volume and was already up 23.8% over 65 sessions, under the line of about 30%. The day-4 reclaim at 357.70 reached only 0.45R. The time stop is built for a trade that goes nowhere.

reasons: the time stop is the owner's rulebook (C33)
the day count is ambiguous in the old question text, now fixed

questions.q: Is it an earnings gapper?
questions.story: GE, 2015. A 5.4% gap on 10.0x volume closes at 90% of its range. The earnings calendar shows no report that day.
choices: Not earnings; find the headline
An earnings gapper; volume says so
An earnings gapper; the close says so
No setup; it was not earnings
questions.answer: Not earnings; find the headline
questions.why: Not earnings. The calendar shows no report that day, so this is a news gap and you need the headline. Calling every big gap earnings without checking is a mistake, since a quarter are not. A strong close shows strength, not the catalyst. The calendar and the headline name the catalyst.
questions.lesson_line: Check the calendar. A quarter of big gaps are not earnings.

wrong.An earnings gapper; volume says so: Volume does not tell you the catalyst. The calendar does.
wrong.An earnings gapper; the close says so: A strong close shows strength, not the catalyst. The calendar does.
wrong.No setup; it was not earnings: A gap with no report is not thrown out. It needs a named headline.

questions.simple: It is not an earnings gap, because no report came out that day, so find the real headline first.

deeper.trap: Calling every big gap earnings without checking is a mistake: a quarter are not. Volume and a strong close do not name a catalyst. The earnings calendar answers the first question, and the headline answers the second.

reasons: tied to held decision D-025 (who owns a no-report news gap)
fixed before

questions.q: How should the light volume change your view?
questions.story: AAPL, 2022. The report was the day before. The stock gaps up 4.1% on 1.7x its 50-day volume and closes at its high.
choices: It lowers the grade; it is no veto
It voids the setup; no trade at all
It makes the gap an even better buy
It only matters on non-report gaps
questions.answer: It lowers the grade; it is no veto
questions.why: It lowers the grade, and it is no veto. For us volume raises the grade and is not a must-have. AAPL gapped on 1.7x the 50-day volume and closed at its high, so it still counts, at a lower grade.
questions.lesson_line: Volume raises the grade. It is not a must-have.

wrong.It voids the setup; no trade at all: Volume is not a requirement for this setup to count. It only raises the grade.
wrong.It makes the gap an even better buy: Light volume does not help. Heavy volume raises the grade.
wrong.It only matters on non-report gaps: Volume raises the grade on every gap. It never decides whether the setup counts.

questions.simple: Light volume lowers the grade but does not cancel the setup. Volume raises the grade and is not a must-have.

deeper.counter: Kullamagi calls volume the number one thing to focus on, and some traders treat it as a must. We say it only raises the grade. AAPL's light volume costs it grade, not its place.

reasons: volume as a grade raiser, not a must, is the owner's ruling D-006
one example from our own scan, not yet owner reviewed

questions.q: Is it a News Failure?
questions.story: NFLX, 2018. A 9.2% gap on 3.3x volume. The low of the day is 35.65, above the prior close of 34.64. It closes at 35% of its range.
choices: No; the gap held and never filled
Yes; any fade is a failure
No; a 35% close is a strong one
Yes; it ended in the lower half
questions.answer: No; the gap held and never filled
questions.why: No. The gap held, since the low of 35.65 stayed above the prior close of 34.64, so it never filled. A News Failure closes under the prior close or trades back to it. This day was a weak, faded close at 35% of its range, not a failure.
questions.lesson_line: A fade that holds the gap is weak, not a News Failure.

wrong.Yes; any fade is a failure: A News Failure closes under the prior close or trades back to it.
wrong.No; a 35% close is a strong one: The answer is no, but not for that reason. A 35% close is in the lower half, a weak close.
wrong.Yes; it ended in the lower half: A weak close is not the failure. A close under the prior close or a filled gap is.

questions.simple: No. The gap held and the day closed above the prior close, so it is a weak close and not a News Failure.

deeper.trap: A weak close is not a close under the prior close. Here the low of 35.65 stayed above the prior close of 34.64, so the gap held. That is a faded day, not a News Failure.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: How does it grade?
questions.story: URI, 2024. A gap on earnings on 4.0x volume, close at 89% of its range, on a stock up 42% over the prior 65 sessions.
choices: Late in a run; a B- at best
A+; 4.0x volume and a high close
Fine; the close is near the high
A+; strength begets strength
questions.answer: Late in a run; a B- at best
questions.why: Late in a run, a B- at best. The stock was up 42% in the prior 65 sessions, past the line of about 30%. A late gap carries the climax risk.
questions.lesson_line: A gap on a stock already up 42% is late.

wrong.A+; 4.0x volume and a high close: Volume and the close are good; the run into the gap is the problem.
wrong.Fine; the close is near the high: A strong day does not erase a 42% run into it.
wrong.A+; strength begets strength: A big run into the gap is the late-gap warning, not a plus.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: PANW, 2021. An 11.6x volume gap held its low through a 6-session pullback. On day 8 the stock trades over the prior day's high at 77.06. The stop goes at 75.92.
choices: Market 77.06; stop 75.92; third at 80.48
Limit 74.00; stop 70.00; hold
Market at close; stop 77.06; 2R
Market 77.06; no stop; third at 10R
questions.answer: Market 77.06; stop 75.92; third at 80.48
questions.why: Market 77.06, stop 75.92, a third at 80.48. One R is the fill minus the stop; three of those above the fill is 80.48. PANW reached 14.2R.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop and first trim, written before the open.

wrong.Limit 74.00; stop 70.00; hold: A limit far below never fills, and a stop that wide breaks the size rule.
wrong.Market at close; stop 77.06; 2R: A stop at the entry is no stop, and the first trim is 3R.
wrong.Market 77.06; no stop; third at 10R: A real stop goes in with the broker, and the first third is at 3R.

questions.q: A pullback that dips under the gap-day midpoint is graded down.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A first pullback that holds the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue. One that dips under the gap-day midpoint is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Holding the upper half is A+. Under the midpoint is a B-.

questions.q: Grade each pullback.
questions.story: Two stocks gap on reports and close strong. The first one's pullback never leaves the upper half of the gap day. The second one's pullback dips under the gap-day midpoint but holds the low.
choices: First an A+ cue; second a B- cue
Both the same; both hold low
First a B- cue; shallow is weak
Second an A+ cue; tested more
questions.answer: First an A+ cue; second a B- cue
questions.why: First an A+ cue, second a B- cue. A first pullback that holds the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue. A pullback that dips under the gap-day midpoint is a B- cue. Both hold the low, so both pass the setup. Depth still shapes the grade.
questions.lesson_line: A shallow pullback grades above a deep one.

wrong.Both the same; both hold low: Both hold the low, but the depth still grades.
wrong.First a B- cue; shallow is weak: A shallow pullback shows strength, not weakness.
wrong.Second an A+ cue; tested more: Dipping under the midpoint is a B- cue, not extra strength.

questions.simple: A pullback that stays in the upper half of the gap day grades higher than one that dips under its midpoint.

deeper.trap: Both pullbacks hold the gap-day low, so a rule-reader may call them equal. But the grade looks at how deep the pullback went. A B- or lower is sized down, while A and B setups take normal size and an A+ is sized up.

reasons: both grade cues come from one criteria card

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A stock has gapped up two days in a row, each on wider ranges. Today a news headline gaps it a third time on 4x volume.
choices: Pass; this is day three of a burst
Pass; headline is not a report
Buy day one; volume is strong
Buy the pullback tomorrow
questions.answer: Pass; this is day three of a burst
questions.why: Pass. Our card wants a gap that is not the 3rd to 5th day of a straight-up burst. This is the third gap. Buying the third gap of a parabolic burst is a mistake. Good volume does not make a late gap early.
questions.lesson_line: The third gap of a burst is late. Pass.

wrong.Pass; headline is not a report: Passing is right, but not for that reason. A named headline can be a catalyst. The third gap of a burst is the problem.
wrong.Buy day one; volume is strong: Good volume does not fix a third gap in a burst.
wrong.Buy the pullback tomorrow: A pullback buy still needs a setup that is not late.

questions.simple: Pass. Today is the third day of a straight-up burst, which is too late to buy.

deeper.trap: Strong volume makes the third gap look fresh. The card asks where the stock is in its run. It should not be the 3rd to 5th day of a straight-up burst. It should not be up more than about 30% in the 65 sessions before the gap.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: How does the volume grade?
questions.story: A stock gaps on a report. By 9:50, twenty minutes after the open, it has already traded its full average daily volume.
choices: An A+ cue: heavy volume early on
A B- cue: 20 minutes is too short
No cue: only the close counts
A cue only if the gap is 10% or more
questions.answer: An A+ cue: heavy volume early on
questions.why: An A+ cue. Volume is A+ when the average daily volume trades in the first 15 to 20 minutes. It is also A+ when it is the highest in a year or ever. Kullamagi: ideally the stock trades the average daily volume in that time or even quicker. Here it did so by 9:50.
questions.lesson_line: A day's average volume in 20 minutes is an A+ cue.

wrong.A B- cue: 20 minutes is too short: Twenty minutes is inside the 15 to 20 minute window, so the cue is already met.
wrong.No cue: only the close counts: Volume early in the day is the point of the cue.
wrong.A cue only if the gap is 10% or more: The volume cue stands on its own. The average daily volume in the first 15 to 20 minutes is an A+ volume cue.

questions.simple: Trading a full day of average volume in the first 20 minutes is an A+ cue for volume.

deeper.trap: The line of 3 times is measured by the close. The stock must be on pace for it by the opening-range buy. This A+ cue is about speed: the average daily volume traded in the first 15 to 20 minutes. A big day that built slowly does not earn this speed cue.

reasons: the cue comes from the card and from Kullamagi's page, two sources that agree

questions.q: May you take the reclaim?
questions.story: You have been stopped out of the same stock three times this week on three clean reclaims. A fourth reclaim triggers on Friday.
choices: No; three tries a week are used
Yes; a new trigger is a new trade
Yes, at half size to cut the risk
No; a stop-out bars it for the week
questions.answer: No; three tries a week are used
questions.why: No. The same stock gets at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month. Three stop-outs this week use the weekly count, so the fourth reclaim waits. After a stop-out, a new trigger is a new trade with its own stop, but it still counts as a try.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week on one stock, then stop.

wrong.Yes; a new trigger is a new trade: A new trigger is a new trade, but the tries per week are capped.
wrong.Yes, at half size to cut the risk: Smaller size does not reopen the tries. The cap is on tries, not on size.
wrong.No; a stop-out bars it for the week: The answer is no, but not for that reason. After a stop-out you may buy again on a new trigger, up to the cap.

questions.simple: No. We allow at most 3 tries a week on one stock, and you have used all 3.

deeper.trap: A new trigger makes it a new trade with its own stop, and that is why the fourth reclaim feels allowed. It does not reset the count of tries on that stock: at most 3 in a week and 6 in a month.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (E56 and B21)

questions.q: Risk formula and position cap both allow 666 shares. The stock is $600, average daily volume 40,000 shares. Shares you may buy?
questions.answer: 400 shares
questions.why: 400 shares. The risk formula and the position cap both allow 666 shares. We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. 1% of 40,000 is 400. The smaller number wins.
questions.lesson_line: Own the smaller of the risk size and 1% of average volume.
questions.simple: 400 shares. We never own more than 1% of average daily volume, and that is smaller than 666.

deeper.trap: The risk formula and the position cap would allow 666 shares. The volume cap is 1% of the stock's average daily volume, so 400 is the most. Without it you would own more than 1% of what the stock trades in a day.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, five sessions after a report gap. Take the reclaim or pass?
choices: Take it; the gap-day low held
Buy at the close; skip the trigger
Pass; the gap-day low gave way
Pass; the gap has already filled
questions.answer: Take it; the gap-day low held
questions.why: Take it. The setup is complete. A 14.2% gap on 4.8x volume closed at 94% of its range. A 4-session pullback, 2.8% deep, held the gap-day low, then reclaimed the prior high. The buy is a market order as price trades over the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: A held gap-day low and a clean reclaim is the setup.

wrong.Pass; the gap-day low gave way: No close in the pullback sat under the gap-day low.
wrong.Pass; the gap has already filled: The pullback was only 2.8% deep against a 14.2% gap, so price never got near the prior close.
wrong.Buy at the close; skip the trigger: The buy is a market order as price trades over the prior day's high. Buying before that skips the trigger.

questions.simple: Take it. The gap was big, volume was heavy, the close was strong, and the pullback held the gap-day low.

deeper.example: March 2016: report on 2016-03-10, gap day 2016-03-11, up 14.2% on 4.8x volume, close at 94% of its range. Day 6: a buy over 190.69 with the stop at 186.55, 2.2% away. It reached 12.1R at best. One example is not a promise, but it shows what a held gap-day low and a clean reclaim can do.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed

questions.q: Hidden ticker, an earnings gap day is the last bar. Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; it was already up too much
Take it; the gap day closed strong
Take it; the volume was heavy
Pass; the volume was too thin
questions.answer: Pass; it was already up too much
questions.why: Pass. The stock was up 42% over the prior 65 sessions, past the line of about 30%. The gap day itself looked strong: 5.5% on 4.0x volume, closing at 89% of its range. A late gap in a stock already run up carries the climax risk.
questions.lesson_line: A big run into the gap is the warning. Pass.

wrong.Take it; the gap day closed strong: A strong close does not erase a big run into the gap.
wrong.Take it; the volume was heavy: Heavy volume does not make a late gap early.
wrong.Pass; the volume was too thin: Volume was 4.0x, above the line of at least 3 times. The failing test is the run-up.

questions.simple: Pass, because the stock had already run up 42% in 65 sessions, and a late gap carries climax risk.

deeper.trap: The trap is a strong day that hides a weak setting. The gap day closed at 89% of its range on 4.0x volume, so it looked good. But the 65 sessions before it, a 42% run, break the not-late line of about 30%. Check the run-up first, then the gap day.

questions.q: Grade this one.
questions.story: Report beats with a raise on accelerating growth. A 12% true gap on the highest volume in a year, closing in the top quarter. It comes out of a 4-month quiet range above a rising 200-day. Green market.
choices: A+; all the main cues line up here
B-; a quiet range lacks momentum
A; the gap must be bigger for A+
B-; the close is not at the high
questions.answer: A+; all the main cues line up here
questions.why: A+. A beat, a raise and accelerating growth, a true gap of 10% or more and the year's top volume line up. So do a top-quarter close and a quiet range above a rising 200-day. An A+ is sized up.
questions.lesson_line: When every cue lines up, size up. That is an A+.

wrong.B-; a quiet range lacks momentum: A quiet range above a rising 200-day is an A+ cue, not a lack of momentum.
wrong.A; the gap must be bigger for A+: The A+ gap is 10% or more, and this one is 12%.
wrong.B-; the close is not at the high: The A+ close is in the top quarter of the range. It need not be at the high.

questions.simple: It is an A+ because the beat and raise, true gap, top volume, strong close and quiet base all line up.

deeper.trap: The grade comes from the cues, not from the entry. When they all line up, as here, an A+ is sized up.

questions.q: Day-one buys and pullback buys share the same trims, trail, breakeven and time stop.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Both share one exit plan. The first sell is a judgment, then the stop goes to breakeven. The rest trails the 9 or 20 EMA. Under 1R after 10 sessions, either one is sold.

questions.q: What must happen before you buy SEDG again?
questions.story: SEDG, 2019. A 15.0% gap on 11.4x volume. You bought the day-4 reclaim at 51.76. It failed the next session and the stop took you out.
choices: A new trigger, as a new trade
Buy it back now; the gap was strong
Stay out of it for a full month
Buy it back at half size to be safe
questions.answer: A new trigger, as a new trade
questions.why: A new trigger, as a new trade. After a stop-out, we buy again only if the setup triggers again. It is a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
questions.lesson_line: After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger.

wrong.Buy it back now; the gap was strong: A strong gap is not a trigger. Only the setup triggering again is.
wrong.Stay out of it for a full month: The rule caps tries, it does not ban the stock: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.
wrong.Buy it back at half size to be safe: Half size does not replace the trigger. A new buy needs its own trigger, stop and size.

questions.simple: After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade with its own stop.

deeper.trap: A big gap on big volume can make a stop-out feel like a mistake. The day-4 reclaim at 51.76 failed the next session, best 0.0R, and the gap was given back within weeks. Whatever the gap looked like, the next buy needs its own new trigger.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed

questions.q: What keeps the plan alive?
questions.story: In our scan of news gappers, roughly three in ten reach 3R before the stop. The rest do not.
choices: Small losses, selling into pushes
A wider stop that rarely gets hit
Adding more when volume climbs fast
Skipping every pullback buy
questions.answer: Small losses, selling into pushes
questions.why: Small losses, and selling into strength. In our scan 29.5% reached 3R and 19.5% reached 5R before the stop, so most buys never get far. The stop sets the size, so each loss is small. The first sell is a judgment, often into a 3, 5 or 7 day push.
questions.lesson_line: Most buys never reach 3R. Small losses and selling into strength keep the plan alive.

wrong.A wider stop that rarely gets hit: The stop sits a few cents under the pullback low and never moves wider. Parking it far away to avoid being hit breaks that rule.
wrong.Adding more when volume climbs fast: One buy, one price, one stop: no adding.
wrong.Skipping every pullback buy: The pullback buy is part of the plan, not the problem.

questions.simple: Small losses at the stop and selling into strength keep the plan alive. Only about three in ten buys reach 3R.

deeper.counter: Three in ten reaching 3R sounds poor. In the scan 29.5% reached 3R and 19.5% reached 5R before the stop, so most buys never reach 3R. The stop sets the size of each loss, and the first sell is a judgment, often into a 3, 5 or 7 day push.

questions.q: In the 60 sessions before a gap, the high was 58.00 and the low was 46.00. How far is the high above the low, in percent?
questions.why: 26.1%. The high minus the low is 58.00 minus 46.00. Divide that by the low, 46.00, and show it as a percent. That is under the 35% line, so the 60 sessions were a quiet range, the setting our card prefers. A base of 4 weeks or more is the card's other preferred setting.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet means the 60-session high is within 35% of the low.
questions.simple: The high is about 26.1% above the low, under the 35% line, so the range was quiet.

questions.q: Which gap has the better setting?
choices: The flat base; it was quiet first
The swinger; it already has momentum
Equal; only the catalyst matters here
Neither; a 12% gap is too small
questions.answer: The flat base; it was quiet first
questions.why: The flat base. UCT prefers a gap out of a base. That means an open above the top of a base of 4 weeks or more, or out of a quiet range. In a quiet range, the prior 60 sessions' high is no more than 35% above their low. The 5-month base fits. The swing from 20.00 to 31.00 is wider than that line. Both gaps are 12%, so the news is not the difference.
questions.lesson_line: Prefer a gap out of a base or a quiet range.

wrong.The swinger; it already has momentum: Our card prefers a quiet range first. A wide swing is not quiet.
wrong.Equal; only the catalyst matters here: The catalyst comes first, but the setting still moves the grade.
wrong.Neither; a 12% gap is too small: A gap of 10% or more is an A+ gap, so 12% is not small.

questions.story: Two stocks gap 12% on the same kind of news. One opens above a flat 5-month base. The other has swung between 20.00 and 31.00 over the last 60 sessions.
questions.simple: The flat base is better. UCT prefers a gap out of a long quiet base over one out of wild swings.

questions.q: How many shares may you own?
choices: 3,000; 1% of the average volume
20,000, since today is heavy volume
60,000, 1% of today's volume
30,000, 10% of the average volume
questions.answer: 3,000; 1% of the average volume
questions.why: 3,000. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. One percent of 300,000 is 3,000. Today's 6 million shares do not lift the cap, because it uses the average. The size is the smaller of the risk-based size and the cap, so 3,000 beats the 20,000 from the stop math.
questions.lesson_line: Cap the size at 1% of average daily volume.

wrong.20,000, since today is heavy volume: A one-day surge does not lift the cap. It uses the average.
wrong.60,000, 1% of today's volume: The cap is 1% of the average daily volume, not of today's.
wrong.30,000, 10% of the average volume: The cap is 1% of the average daily volume. Ten percent is far over it.

questions.story: A news gapper averages 300,000 shares a day but trades 6 million today. Your stop math says 20,000 shares.
questions.simple: The cap is 1% of the average daily volume, which is 3,000 shares, not a share of today's surge.

questions.q: You bought at 80.00 with the stop at 77.00. A gap-down day's first 30-minute low is 71.00. What is the loss, in R?
questions.answer: 3R
questions.why: 3R. One R is the buy minus the original stop, 80.00 minus 77.00. The loss to the low is 80.00 minus 71.00. Divide that loss by one R to get 3R, past the 2R ceiling. If the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: First 30 minutes past 2R: get out.
questions.simple: 3R. The loss to the first 30-minute low is three times the original risk, which is past 2R, so you get out.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (B20 gap rule)

choices: 3R
1R
2R

wrong.1R: Counted only the original risk, not the whole loss.
wrong.2R: Measured from the stop, not from the buy.
wrong.0.3R: Flipped the division: one R over the loss.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Make 75.50 the stop and stay in
Sell at once; news gappers gap again
Drop the stop to 74.00 to give it room
Move the stop to breakeven, 80.00
questions.answer: Make 75.50 the stop and stay in
questions.why: Make 75.50 the stop and stay in. After a gap through the stop, the low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop. You get out only if that low takes the loss past 2R. Here the loss is 1.5R. News stocks gap again, but the rule is the number, not the headline.
questions.lesson_line: News stocks gap again. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at once; news gappers gap again: You get out only if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R. Here they do not.
wrong.Drop the stop to 74.00 to give it room: The stop moves only by the gap rule: the first 30-minute low, 75.50, not a level picked for room.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven, 80.00: Breakeven comes with a trim at 2R to 5R, not on a loss. The gap rule sets the new stop at the first 30-minute low.

questions.story: You bought at 80.00 with the stop at 77.00. Follow-up news gaps the stock open at 75.80. The first 30-minute low is 75.50, a loss of 1.5R.
questions.simple: Make 75.50 the new stop and stay in, because the loss at that low is only 1.5R, under the 2R ceiling.

deeper.trap: Selling at once feels safe, but the rule is a number. The first 30-minute low becomes the new stop. Only a loss past 2R in those 30 minutes means get out. Here the loss is 1.5R, so you stay in.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B20 gap rule)

questions.q: What is a PEG?
choices: A leader's report gap, clearing a base
First gap in six months, neglected stock
Small gap after a weak red close
Gap up on good news, then a red close

wrong.Gap up on good news, then a red close: That is a News Failure: it closes red after good news.
wrong.Small gap after a weak red close: That is a Kicker: a small gap after a weak red close, rarely on a headline.

questions.q: What is Gap Support?
choices: A later test of the gap-up low itself
First pullback after a gap, in days
Gap up on good news, red close
Stop placed under the gap-up low
questions.answer: A later test of the gap-up low itself
questions.why: A later test of the gap-up low itself. Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low, 2 to 60 sessions on, bought as that low is defended. The gapper's own pullback comes within about 2 to 10 sessions and keeps every close above the gap-day low.

wrong.Gap up on good news, red close: That is a News Failure: it closes red after good news.
wrong.Stop placed under the gap-up low: Gap Support is a later test of the gap-up low, bought as that low is defended. It is not a stop level.
